summary_plain: This experiment tested whether a modified smoke and particle counter could operate reliably in microgravity aboard the International Space Station. Researchers used aerosol standards and dust to evaluate the device and ensure future spacecraft fire detection systems would work properly. The findings help secure reliable smoke and aerosol monitoring for astronaut safety.
summary_expert: The Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT / DAFT-2) was conducted to mitigate risks for the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) by testing a modified TSI P-Trak condensation nuclei counter in microgravity. The P-Trak was modified with a redesigned condenser tube using capillary forces to recycle isopropyl alcohol and by removing its gravitational tilt switch. Test variables included sampling Arizona Road Dust (ARD) aerosols contained in 15-liter Mylar bags and cabin air generated by actions such as Velcro demates, comparing P-Trak particle counts against a TSI DustTrak laser scattering control. On-orbit test point 2 data showed P-Trak readings responding well above 30,000 pt/cc during Velcro dust generation, and flight data indicated that count-to-mass ratios clustered differently than ground tests due to a higher proportion of larger particles remaining entrained without gravitational settling.

key_findings.text: During flight testing, test point #2 data demonstrated that the P-Trak responded to Velcro dust with several readings above the 30,000 pt/cc mark while remaining within its prescribed maximum count of 500,000 pt/cc.

On-orbit data acquired from the aerosol tests fell outside ground-based relationships, clustering in a region where the count/mass ratio is lower than determined from ground testing, indicating that the mass of the average particle counted on orbit is higher due to a lack of gravitational settling.

Testing showed that the DAFT Impactor, designed to filter out larger particles, was only about 50% efficient, allowing a considerable number of larger particles to be drawn into the measurement devices.
